summary: At just 1.3 square miles, Camino Tassajara is one of the smallest census-designated places in the East Bay's Tri-Valley corridor, yet it commands a median home value that tops two million dollars — an 8-to-1 price-to-income ratio even against a median household income exceeding $250,000, which means that purchasing here requires substantial wealth even by Bay Area standards. Tucked into the rolling, golden-grass hills east of San Ramon and in the shadow of Mount Diablo, the terrain is distinctly hilly, with ridgeline views that shift from amber to violet at sunset and open-sky sightlines that feel surprisingly rural for a place minutes from Interstate 680. This is firmly a bedroom community; the Tri-Valley's major employers in tech, engineering, and healthcare (concentrated in Pleasanton, Dublin, and Livermore) sit within a short commute, but Camino Tassajara itself offers almost no commercial employment base. With 9.5 hours of average daily sunshine and highs hovering near 70°F year-round, the climate is classic inland Contra Costa — warm and dry summers, mild winters, negligible fog. The single school serving the area posts ELA scores 79 points above standard and math scores 69 points above, numbers that rank among the highest in the state. The tradeoff is stark: extraordinary residential polish in exchange for driving virtually everywhere, since retail, dining, and daily errands cluster in neighboring cities rather than within this tiny footprint.
